title: Avoided crossings in spin-boson systems: consequences for adiabatic state preparation
authors: Joona Marjamäki, Robert van Leeuwen, Riku Tuovinen
abstract: Avoided crossings in the correlated many-body spectrum play a central role in determining the conditions for adiabatic state preparation in interacting quantum systems. We investigate this connection in finite spin-boson systems by combining exact diagonalization of the many-body spectrum with time-dependent simulations of adiabatic switching protocols. By comparing the adiabatically prepared state with the exact ground state, we determine the switching times required for reliable preparation as a function of the spin-boson coupling strength and bosonic mode structure. We show that regions of small many-body level spacings, associated with avoided crossings, impose the strongest constraints on adiabatic preparation and explain the observed dependence of the required switching times on the interaction strength. Furthermore, while the ground-state energy follows the overall spectral trends, local observables such as Pauli matrix expectation values exhibit additional non-monotonic behavior arising from coherent oscillations in finite systems. These findings can provide concrete benchmarks for both the theoretical treatment of open quantum systems and practical implementations in quantum simulation and qubit control.
summary: This paper analyzes adiabatic state preparation in spin-boson systems by examining the role of avoided crossings in the many-body energy spectrum. Using exact diagonalization and time-dependent simulations, the authors show that the required switching time is dictated by the smallest spectral gaps. They highlight that local observables can reveal dynamics that are slower or behave differently than the overall ground-state energy evolution.
main_problem: The paper investigates the conditions required for reliable adiabatic state preparation in interacting quantum systems, focusing specifically on the role of avoided crossings in the many-body spectrum.
main_result: Avoided crossings impose the strongest constraints on adiabatic preparation, dictating the minimum required switching times. Furthermore, local observables can exhibit non-monotonic behavior, suggesting that state preparation fidelity depends on the observable measured.
method: The authors combine exact diagonalization of the many-body spectrum with time-dependent simulations of adiabatic switching protocols to benchmark preparation success.
model_or_system: The system studied is the spin-boson model, which couples a two-level system (qubit) to a bosonic environment (bath). The Hamiltonian includes terms for the qubit, the bath, and the coupling interaction.
key_observables: Adiabatic preparation success (comparing prepared state to exact ground state), many-body level spacings, local observables (e.g., Pauli matrix expectation values), and required switching times ($t_0$).
important_parameters: Spin-boson coupling strength ($\gamma$), qubit tunneling amplitude ($\epsilon$), and the structure of the bosonic bath (single vs. three modes).
main_assumptions: The analysis uses a finite bosonic environment, allowing for exact diagonalization, which differs from standard continuum bath approximations. The study also notes that the required time depends on the specific observable used for convergence checking.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the single-mode energy spectrum showing avoided crossings, the dependence of required switching times on coupling strength ($\gamma$) for various $\epsilon$, and comparisons of state evolution using different observables ($\langle\sigma_zangle$ vs $\langle\sigma_xangle$).
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the theoretical framework using the spin-boson model and the adiabatic condition. It then numerically simulates the switching process, comparing results for global quantities (ground state energy) versus local observables (Pauli expectation values) across different coupling regimes.
why_interesting: This work provides concrete, quantitative benchmarks for understanding how spectral features like avoided crossings limit the speed of quantum control protocols in open quantum systems, which is highly relevant to superconducting qubits and quantum simulation.
